items.title: Herdr
items.description: (GitHub, herdr-app, herdr-core, TUI docs) - Apache-2.0 desktop app, terminal UI and runtime where Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other coding-agent CLIs run as real terminals in herdr-core and keep running after the window closes. The app and the original Herdr TUI do not share agents; a reboot ends running programs, and app releases send usage telemetry by default.

Self-hosting runs the app and API on your server; session computers and Drive stay on Platinum sandboxes.

repo_info.description: Kortix CompanyOS – the open-source operating system for your company. Multiplayer AI agents, your company as code, sovereign on your infrastructure or ours.

items.title: Sno Station
items.description: (GitHub, Install) - Apache-2.0 local layer that turns Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw on one computer into a squad: when one agent hits its rate limit, another picks up the task from the same memory and mailbox with context intact, and either agent can review the other's work, with the reviewer always a different agent. Memory is encrypted locally, and messages and skills live on the machine; no daemon or server is needed. A nightly Self Learning job proposes skill changes that apply only after the user accepts them. Linux and macOS. REM Enhanced sends memory text to Sno's cloud; Agent Native uploads sessions nightly for Self Learning by default unless disabled, while Local First does not upload memory text.

repo_info.description: When Claude Code hits its usage limit, Codex picks the task up from the same memory. Sno Station puts Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw on one squad: they hand work to each other and review each other's code. Open source, runs on your computer.

items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - MIT-licensed VS Code-core editor that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kimi and other ACP agents in per-chat worktrees and sandboxes, with subagents, hunk-level keep/undo and per-turn Git checkpoints.

repo_info.description: The best open-source Agentic development environment.

items.title: Kraft
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - Apache-2.0 local orchestrator that runs each task from spec to pull request in its own git worktree, so tasks run in parallel: steps run in order from a YAML chain file, tests and CI are checked in steps of their own, attempts and spend are capped, and a person approves the spec, the plan and the final review from the web UI, a phone or the CLI. Claude Code by default; Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Amp and Antigravity can run steps.

repo_info.description: A local orchestrator that takes your coding agent from spec to pull request, stopping only when a decision is yours.

items.title: AIWorks
items.description: (README, Runbook) - MIT-licensed supervisor for one Windows PC that runs Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor through an approved plan in isolated git worktrees, has a separate session verify each step, and delivers pull requests to GitHub; it keeps going through crashes, restarts, and usage limits and asks the owner only for decisions. Early preview; real worker execution is Windows-only, and the synthetic-data dashboard demo also runs on Linux and macOS.

repo_info.description: Manager for AI coding agents that runs on your own PC: hands each step of an agreed plan to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, has a second AI verify the result, and delivers pull requests to GitHub. Keeps going through crashes, restarts and usage limits; asks you only for real decisions. Windows, early preview.

items.description: Frameworks and product surfaces for creating agents, teams, workflows, chatflows, agent apps, or production agent runtimes.

items.title: OpenClaw
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed assistant. A local Gateway on your computer answers in the chat apps and native apps you connect, and it can connect to MCP servers.

repo_info.description: The AI that really does things. Any OS. Any Platform. The lobster way. 🦞

items.title: Hermes Agent
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed agent from Nous Research. One loop serves the terminal, a messaging gateway, cron, and an editor bridge, and connects MCP servers you add.

repo_info.description: The agent that grows with you

items.title: Dify
items.description: (GitHub) - Agentic workflow builder that combines workflows, chatflows, apps, and knowledge systems.

repo_info.description: Build Agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, with rich AI model and tool support on one collaborative workspace. Deploy on cloud, VPC, or self-hosted, so teams move from prototype to production without rebuilding the stack.

items.title: Flowise
items.description: (GitHub) - Visual builder for AI agents and orchestration flows.

repo_info.description: Build AI Agents, Visually

items.title: LangGraph
items.description: (Multi-agent docs) - MIT-licensed low-level orchestration framework for durable, stateful agents and custom multi-agent graph composition. Also supports single-agent workflows; not an out-of-box coding-team runner, and optional LangSmith services are separate from the open-source core.

repo_info.description: Build resilient agents.

items.title: Agno
items.description: (GitHub) - Production runtime for agentic software with agents, teams, workflows, and AgentOS services.

repo_info.description: The self-managing agent platform

items.title: NanoClaw
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - MIT-licensed assistant. A Node host routes chat into a Linux container per agent. qwibitai/nanoclaw redirects to nanocoai/nanoclaw. Agents do not hold raw API keys.

repo_info.description: A lightweight alternative to OpenClaw that runs in containers for security. Connects to WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Gmail and other messaging apps,, has memory, scheduled jobs, and runs directly on Anthropic's Agents SDK

items.title: Sim
items.description: (GitHub) - Apache-2.0 workspace for agent workflows in the browser or a Mac app. A deployed workflow can run as an API or as MCP tools, and workflows can call external MCP servers. The Chat service still uses a key from sim.ai.

repo_info.description: Sim is the collaborative workspace to build, deploy, and monitor AI agents and workflows. Used by 100,000+ builders.

items.title: Mastra
items.description: (GitHub) - TypeScript framework for agents, graph-based workflows, MCP servers, evals, observability, and production AI applications.

repo_info.description: Mastra is the modern TypeScript framework for AI-powered applications and agents.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework
items.description: (Workflow samples) - MIT-licensed Python/.NET developer framework for sequential, concurrent, handoff, and group-collaboration workflows with streaming, checkpoints, and human input. Developers implement and test the application and configure providers; not a ready-made parallel coding-agent workspace.

repo_info.description: A framework for building, orchestrating and deploying AI agents and multi-agent workflows with support for Python and .NET.

items.title: Google AX
items.description: (GitHub, Concepts) - Apache-2.0 declarative orchestrator from Google that runs sandboxed agent tasks at scale on Kubernetes through kubectl-style Task, Workspace, and Model manifests, with suspend and resume, shell access into running sandboxes, and per-workspace repos, MCP servers, and tools. Requires a cluster with Agent Substrate; the README warns of heavy development and likely breaking changes before a stable release.

repo_info.description: Agent Executor (AX) is Google's open agentic orchestration runtime

items.title: Raven
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - Apache-2.0 host agent that plans complex tasks as DAGs and orchestrates built-in research, coding, design, and on-call agents plus 13 third-party agent presets, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent, over ACP, CLI, or OpenAI-compatible APIs.

repo_info.description: The Harness of Harnesses • Super Agent: a trusted, persistent, self-evolving multi-agent ecosystem for all-domain collaboration.

items.title: Cabinet
items.description: (GitHub) - AI-first knowledge base where files live on disk and agents help with execution.

repo_info.description: AI-first knowledge base and startup OS

items.title: Agent Swarm
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - MIT-licensed lead/worker orchestration framework where a lead agent receives tasks from Slack, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira, email, WhatsApp, or the API and delegates to worker agents running in isolated Docker environments with persistent vector-searchable memory, DAG workflows with HITL gates, scheduled tasks, MCP servers, and harness-agnostic execution across Claude Code, Codex, pi-mono, Devin, Claude Managed Agents, and opencode.

repo_info.description: Your Company Agentic Operating System

items.title: SwarmClaw
items.description: (GitHub) - Self-hosted AI agent runtime for autonomous agents, delegated work, schedules, provider management, and chat-platform connectors.

repo_info.description: Open-source self-hosted AI agent runtime and multi-agent framework for autonomous agent swarms. Agent memory, MCP tools, schedules, delegation, and 23+ LLM providers (Claude, GPT, Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama). A practical Claude Code and LangChain alternative.

items.title: AgenticOS
items.description: (Docs) - Apache-2.0 self-hosted platform where a company builds, shares and governs its agents in the browser: agents can delegate to other agents, start on schedules or events, answer in web chat, Slack or the API, and each run is checked against budgets and approval rules and kept in an audit log. Built on Pydantic AI; runs with Docker Compose.

repo_info.description: Open-source, self-hosted AI agent platform for your company's AI teammates. Build, run and govern agents on your own servers and models: shared chat, RAG, skills, a real browser, 4,700+ MCP servers, budgets, approvals and an audit trail. An alternative to ChatGPT Enterprise and Grok Bot. Apache-2.0, built on Pydantic AI.

items.title: apowerb
items.description: (Docs) - Apache-2.0 self-hosted platform where agents are defined in a web UI or REST API and run on ADK with any model through LiteLLM: single, sequential, parallel or loop agents, with retrieval, Text-to-SQL and MCP tools, triggered on demand, by email or on a schedule, and metered against token quotas with a per-session audit log. Runs with Docker Compose or Helm; a few add-ons such as billing and identity-provider sign-in are sold separately.

repo_info.description: The open-source agentic framework to build, orchestrate, and operate production AI agents.

items.title: Agent Office Suite
items.description: (GitHub, Manpo X) - Self-hosted office suite where agents collaborate with humans on docs, databases, slides, and flowcharts through MCP, contextual comments, version history, and traceable edits.

repo_info.description: AOSE — An Office Suite Built for Agent Collaboration. Docs, tables, slides, flowcharts, canvas, and video — all editable by both humans and AI agents.

items.title: NarraNexus
items.description: Open-source AI agent team workspace by NetMind.AI whose agents remember, collaborate, and use tools from day one.

repo_info.description: A framework for building nexuses of agents -- where intelligence emerges from interaction, not isolation.

items.title: Reliant
items.description: (GitHub, Workflows docs, License) - Source-available, not OSI open source (BSL 1.1; each release converts to Apache-2.0 four years after publication) agent harness where coding-agent workflows are YAML graphs versioned in the repo: agent, shell, approval and integration steps joined by conditional edges, started by hand, on a schedule, or by GitHub, Slack, Gmail or Twilio events. Built-in workflows cycle through implementing, checking and reviewing until lint, tests and build pass, or run three agents in separate git worktrees and have a reviewer pick or merge the result, and agents can spawn sub-agents. Runs on your own computer with your own model keys, or on paid Reliant cloud machines that keep working after the laptop closes; desktop and web apps.

repo_info.description: A complete agentic environment with remote connections, workflow-based chats, and more

items.title: Agon
items.description: (Paper) - Autonomous research system that coordinates scientist, coder, and auditor loops from topic to idea, proposal, experiment, and paper.

repo_info.description: Claude Code plugin for autonomous AI research — multi-agent loops take a bare topic all the way to running experiments, with no human-written experimental code.

items.title: Crewplane
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - Apache-2.0 orchestrator that turns Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, and other command-line agents into structured, repeatable Markdown workflows with resumable execution and inspectable local run records.

repo_info.description: Run reviewable, resumable coding-agent workflows across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, GitHub Copilot CLI, or any CLI. You define the stages in Markdown; Crewplane runs the workflow, agents do the work, and every handoff stays on disk.

items.title: Sorcerer
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed native macOS app that orchestrates a community of persona agents with memory and relationships reacting to a "what if...?" scenario, with injectable events, forkable branches, polls and reports, on Claude Code, Codex CLI or local Ollama.

repo_info.description: Simulate communities of AI agents around a “what if…?” question. Native, local-first macOS app (SwiftUI) that runs on the Claude, ChatGPT/Codex or Ollama you already use. Free and open source.

items.title: Multi-Agent Platforms And Builders

items.description: Systems where the central object is the team, company, room, protocol, role, goal, job, or handoff layer between agents.

items.title: Paperclip
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed control plane. Agents wake on heartbeats, a task checks out with a lock, and budgets and approvals are recorded. One deployment can hold several organizations.

repo_info.description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work

items.title: Ruflo
items.description: (Swarm plugin docs) - MIT-licensed coding-agent meta-harness, formerly Claude Flow, for coordinated Claude Code and Codex swarms with team topologies, messaging, and per-agent worktrees. Lite plugins differ from full CLI initialization, which writes configuration/hooks and registers MCP; swarm plugin compatibility and early-access hook requirements apply.

repo_info.description: 🌊 The original agent harness. Deploy intelligent multi-player swarms, coordinate autonomous workflows, and build conversational AI systems. Features adaptive memory, self-learning intelligence, federation, vector RAG integration, and native Claude Code / Codex / Hermes and many more Integrated

items.title: CrewAI
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed Python framework. Crews are role and task JSON. Flows are event-driven Python that can call those crews. Agents can attach MCP servers.

repo_info.description: Framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents. By fostering collaborative intelligence, CrewAI empowers agents to work together seamlessly, tackling complex tasks.

items.title: OpenRig
items.description: (README) - Apache-2.0 local team coordination through YAML RigSpecs, native coding agents in tmux, messaging, and topology snapshot/restore. Requires Node.js 22 or 24 and tmux on macOS/Linux; setup/startup can write provider hooks and trust settings beyond what dry-run previews.

repo_info.description: Build your own network of agents from Claude Code, Codex and Pi: persistent teams with roles, shared context and owned work.

items.title: Commonly
items.description: (GitHub) - Apache-2.0 pods where a team's people and the agents each person runs (Claude Code or Codex from a Mac, or a hosted agent) share conversations and one task board, claim tasks, and send decision cards to a person.

repo_info.description: One pod for your team and the agents each of you runs: your own Claude Code, or a hosted agent in one click. Open source (Apache-2.0), self-hostable.

items.title: Concord MCP
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed TypeScript stdio MCP server () for local-first shared work-state for coding agents: presence, file claims, messaging, handoffs and review packets, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents can coordinate on one repo.

repo_info.description: Live messaging for coding agents

items.title: Sno Station
items.description: (GitHub, Install) - Apache-2.0 local layer that turns Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw on one computer into a squad: when one agent hits its rate limit, another picks up the task from the same memory and mailbox with context intact, and either agent can review the other's work, with the reviewer always a different agent. Memory is encrypted locally, and messages and skills live on the machine; no daemon or server is needed. A nightly Self Learning job proposes skill changes that apply only after the user accepts them. Linux and macOS. REM Enhanced sends memory text to Sno's cloud; Agent Native uploads sessions nightly for Self Learning by default unless disabled, while Local First does not upload memory text.

repo_info.description: When Claude Code hits its usage limit, Codex picks the task up from the same memory. Sno Station puts Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw on one squad: they hand work to each other and review each other's code. Open source, runs on your computer.

items.title: kwant
items.description: (GitHub) - AGPL-3.0 self-hosted team of AI bots in one Rust binary: bots share spaces, hand work to each other with @mentions, run routines, and ask before anything risky. Runs as a Mac, Linux or Windows (beta) app or on a VPS, with local models or your own provider accounts.

repo_info.description: Your own team of AI bots in one self-hosted binary: spaces, every account you have, handoffs, approvals and routines. Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot, Claude Duet and OpenAI dots. Rust + React.

items.title: Markus
items.description: (GitHub) - Apache-2.0 AI workforce platform for building and running teams of AI agents, with role-based agents, task delegation, shared context, and human oversight of the team's work.

repo_info.description: The all-in-one AI workforce platform, to build AI agent teams. You are the boss.

items.title: Culture
items.description: (GitHub) - Coordination-oriented system with rooms, protocol docs, agent lifecycle patterns, and multiple clients.

repo_info.description: CULTURE.DEV — the professional workspace for agents: CLI, agent harnesses, and the AgentIRC mesh.

items.title: Okto Nexus
items.description: (GitHub) - Elastic-2.0 local-first MCP coordination hub where agents get durable identities, messaging, single-winner handoff claims, and human-in-the-loop approval on risky actions.

repo_info.description: Local-first MCP coordination hub for multi-agent teams, with durable messaging, handoffs, governance, and observability.

items.title: Crewly
items.description: (Website) - MIT-licensed local platform that runs a team of role-based agents (developer, QA, PM, orchestrator) on Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI, with task delegation through agent skills, shared persistent memory, and a web dashboard of live agent terminals. OpenCode also works. Requires one of these agent CLIs installed and logged in.

repo_info.description: Build a team of Claude Code / Codex-CLI / Gemini-CLI for your work

items.title: Tale
items.description: (Project agents, Harnesses) - MIT-licensed project workspace for assigning tasks to reusable AI agents, running coding harnesses in persistent sandboxes, and reviewing reports and deliverables; delegation and review require explicit permissions.

repo_info.description: Open-source project workspace for teams and AI agents. Assign tasks, coordinate agents in persistent sandboxes, and review results together. Self-hosted or managed cloud.

items.title: Isomux
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - Source-available (BSL 1.1, free for organizations of up to 10 people) self-hosted web office for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode agents: each agent keeps a name, instructions, and memory across sessions, agents message each other and share rooms and a task board, and several people can talk to the same agents from any device.

repo_info.description: Give your agents a cute office. Multi-device, multi-user, multi-agent collaboration.

items.title: solveathome
items.description: (GitHub, Data dumps) - MIT-licensed open platform where people set research directions on open problems, their own AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, or anything that can fetch a URL) do the research on their own machines, other contributors' agents check the results, and trusted human reviewers accept or reject them, one vote per person; every result, review, and transcript is public.

repo_info.description: MIT framework for a swarm of AI agents, owned by many people, working one open problem. Strangers' agents check the work. Credit follows the proof.

items.title: Squad
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed alpha. Specialist agents are files in the repo, run through GitHub Copilot or another host added with a flag. The conversation log is separate from the editor.

repo_info.description: Squad: AI agent teams for any project

items.title: Bunkhouse
items.description: AGPL-3.0 AI employees for main-street business with a company inbox, org chart, and governed procedures.

repo_info.description: Open-source AI employees for main-street business. Hire hands that live in your inbox.

items.title: workkit
items.description: Claude Code plugin where a manager agent runs GitHub Issues as the work queue, dispatching scout, worker and verifier subagents per issue and parking results for human QA.

repo_info.description: The issue-pipeline workflow system as a Claude Code plugin: GitHub Issues as the work-item SSOT, labels as the pipeline, guard hooks, a manager crew, and the skills from build to ship.

items.title: STARK OS
items.description: (User guide) - MIT-licensed, self-hosted team of seven role-based agents for social media (director, copywriter, community manager, researcher, video planner, red team, publisher), each with its own prompt, tools, memory and free OpenRouter model; agents delegate and run parallel team reviews with a red-team challenge, and publishing uses per-post human approval or an explicitly enabled Autopilot trust level, with sensitive topics and failed checks held for review.

repo_info.description: Free, self-hosted AI social media manager. Talk to Vision and Wanda in English or Urdu, with seven specialist agents that draft, check, schedule and publish to 12 platforms on free AI models. Nothing goes out without your approval.

items.title: Sqwakie
items.description: (GitHub) - Source-available (FSL-1.1-ALv2, converts to Apache-2.0) coordination layer for a team's coding agents across machines: agents post, reply, subscribe and ask each other from the CLI or as MCP tools over a signed, append-only team log replicated peer-to-peer (built on iroh, or over Tailscale), with a live Mission Control dashboard and kanban project boards whose cards agents can start, review and finish. Setup connects Claude Code and Codex; macOS on Apple Silicon and Linux.

repo_info.description: A walkie-talkie for your team's AI agents: see every Claude Code and Codex agent live, let agents ask each other over MCP, project boards with Data Rooms, seats, peer-to-peer Sqwakie Direct, pooled local LLMs. FSL-1.1-ALv2.

items.title: Coterie
items.description: (README, INSTALL) - Apache-2.0 self-hosted team of persistent Claude Code agents on one Debian host: each agent has its own Unix account and terminal, boots from a shared MCP memory server (identity, team state and unread mail, with a hashed manifest of what it was sent), and gets maildir mail that rings its terminal when idle; a browser page shows every agent's pane. Installs with one pasted line and a guided setup; needs a Claude Code login per agent, and setup writes a dispatch block into each agent's CLAUDE.md and hooks into its settings.

repo_info.description: Self-host a team of persistent Claude Code agents: each with its own Linux account, shared memory, mail between them, and a multi-pane browser page to interact with each agent.

items.title: Coordination And Team Systems

items.title: Multica
items.description: (GitHub, License) - Source-available, not OSI open source: Apache 2.0 plus conditions that require a commercial license for hosted or embedded third-party use and keep Multica branding; included because it is a managed agents platform where coding agents act like teammates, take issues, and reuse shared skills.

repo_info.description: Make humans and AI agents work as one team — open-source and self-hostable.

items.title: Open Swarm
items.description: (GitHub, Releases) - Mac desktop on a waitlist. The homepage says many agents work at once, and each one gets its own browser, apps, and tools. The repository holds signed builds. This version and later are proprietary. Versions published before 8 September 2026 stay AGPL-3.0.

repo_info.description: Signed builds of OpenSwarm

items.title: Joxo
items.description: (GitHub, Supported agents) - Closed-source, hosted; the public repository holds its Claude Code and Codex plugin. One shared project for the coding agents each teammate runs on their own computer (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and others): a task board where a task has one holder at a time, decisions every agent reads, and handoffs that carry the branch and commit.

repo_info.description: Team workspace for AI coding agents: your Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode agents share one project, task board and handoffs. Desktop, iPhone and MCP server.

items.title: Not Open But Important

items.description: Tools that manage parallel CLI-agent sessions, terminals, issue boards, worktrees, diffs, and local review loops. These are useful for agentic coding work, but they are tracked separately from orchestrator/player entries when they do not manage agent teams or runtime behavior directly.

items.title: agent-manager
items.description: (GitHub) - Apache-2.0 terminal UI for macOS and Linux (Windows via WSL2) where Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, and other coding-agent CLIs run side by side in persistent tmux sessions, with live status, prompts sent without attaching, optional per-session Git worktrees, and diff review that sends line comments back to the agent.

repo_info.description: Terminal multiplexer for AI coding agents. Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and more side by side in one tmux TUI, with live status, worktrees and diff review. Discord: discord.gg/ecS88An7pF

items.title: Coven
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - MIT-licensed local-first Rust daemon and CLI that runs Codex, Claude Code, and other coding-agent harnesses as PTY sessions inside explicit project-root boundaries, with SQLite-persisted history and a versioned local socket API.

repo_info.description: Local-first runtime for project-scoped AI coding-agent sessions, with durable state, authority boundaries, and multi-harness interoperability.

items.title: Caprock
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - Apache-2.0 local desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux where Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI sessions run side by side, showing which agent is waiting on you, what each session and pull request cost at API list prices, and how close the plan limits are; an iPhone companion paired by QR answers approvals, and a read-only MCP server lets agents query past sessions and spend. No account and no telemetry.

repo_info.description: Agentic development environment: run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI side by side, and follow every PR from agent to release with its cost. Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, plus a Claude Code plugin. Local, free.

items.title: SuperAgent
items.description: (Website, Releases) - MIT-licensed macOS workspace where Claude Code and Codex run as per-project chats, each on its own git worktree, with a real browser the agent drives on the user's existing logins, a dedicated iOS Simulator per chat for build-install-screenshot loops, scheduled routines, and an iPhone companion paired over an end-to-end encrypted relay for approving tool calls remotely.

repo_info.description: Free, open-source Mac app for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity. Your AI coding agent with a real browser, iOS Simulator, parallel chats on git worktrees, and an iPhone app. No API key.

items.title: Yardlet
items.description: (GitHub) - MIT-licensed native macOS app that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, and other coding-agent CLIs side by side with their own sign-in, where tasks can read, message, and hand work to tasks on other agents, with usage limits across several accounts, MCP connectors shared by every agent, and a built-in browser the agents drive.

repo_info.description: Lightweight, non-intrusive, yet versatile ADE. Run Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity side by side in one native Mac app, with no hooks, no wrappers and nothing written into their settings.

items.title: Brow
items.description: (Website) - GPL-3.0 macOS app for running parallel Claude Code sessions on a multi-repo project: its menu-bar Workspaces gives each feature one folder holding a git worktree of every chosen repository, all on one branch, and moves a session to another Claude account, while the MacBook notch shows every account's 5-hour and weekly limits. Requires macOS 26+ on Apple silicon.

repo_info.description: Claude Code usage limits in the MacBook notch, and workspaces for parallel sessions. Every Claude account's 5-hour and weekly limits and resets at a glance, git-worktree workspaces across several repositories (formerly Grove), and Glim, a small pet that eats your limits. macOS app.

items.title: SpaceApp
items.description: (GitHub, Docs) - Open-source (MIT), self-hosted web workspace where OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and other coding-agent CLIs run side by side as terminal panes in persistent rooms, with MCP servers, managed browser panes, a Room Agent for coordinating work across panes, and a one-command Docker installer () for Linux, macOS, and Windows 11.

repo_info.description: Self-hosted workspace that runs several AI coding CLIs (OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini) side by side in persistent rooms.

items.title: Alchemist Coder
items.description: (Website, README) - AGPL-3.0 desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux that runs Claude Code and Codex over the Agent Client Protocol with a live tree of agents and subagents, inline permissions and diffs, an Arena where one to four agents solve the same approved plan in separate git worktrees before you merge one, and a standing coordinator that hands assignments to an organization of agents. Also indexes Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build history into a read-only local search. The free Community edition runs agents only on local models (Ollama, LM Studio); builds are not code-signed yet.

repo_info.description: Free, open-source desktop app for Claude Code and Codex: follow every agent and subagent live, run your own agent organization and automate routines. Also searches your Gemini CLI and Grok history. macOS, Windows, Linux.

repo_info.description: AI Agent Governance Toolkit — Policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, execution sandboxing, and reliability engineering for autonomous AI agents. Covers 10/10 OWASP Agentic Top 10.
